name: Mitsui & Co.
headline: A Japanese trading house whose low-cost Australian iron-ore mines earned excellent returns through the cycle.
what_short: Japanese trading house with iron ore and gas
what_it_does: Mitsui & Co. is a Japanese trading company with many businesses. The part that carries its profits is mineral and metal resources, led by low-cost iron ore from Australia's Pilbara region, and it also earns from gas and other resources.
why_it_passed: Its iron ore is among the lowest-cost in the world, which protects it when prices fall.
Its returns across a full commodity cycle were excellent.
No doubt about honesty was found in the record the analysis read.
The volume and cost of its main mines are foreseeable, even though the price of ore is not.
why_not_now: At ¥4,775 a share, the price sits near the top of the analysis's value range (¥2,723 to ¥4,796). The analysis found an expected return of only 2.8% to 4.9% a year, below the roughly 10% the analysis requires and below the 4.14% a 30-year Japanese government bond pays at the low end.
watch: The price of ore and gas sets most of its cash, and no one in the business will forecast it.
The accounts feature an adjusted cash figure and guidance, and show recurring write-downs; the analysis weighed these against.
It carries about ¥4.46 trillion of net debt.
